utterances.text: This set of documents also contains a record of the hearing of Dr. Smilja Avramov, in the case against Slobodan Milosevic before this court, who explained how the Serbian academic scientific elite perceived the right to self-determination, but regrettably we shall have no time to deal with that in more detail, but the document is D -- 4D1453. So 4D1453 is the document where you can obtain additional information. General, what I feel is very important in the political principles of the Coalition of National Agreement is to explain -- is to compare items 2 and item 3. Item 2 refers to Croats outside Croatia but in the republics of the former Yugoslavia; and item 3 refers to Croats abroad. Let us now read item 2 carefully. It emanates from this item that it is indubitable that the Croats in the neighbouring republics in the former Yugoslavia should be citizens loyal to the republic in which, as a sovereign state, they live as its citizens.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was this ever in dispute as a concept or as a political idea in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. As you can see, he enjoys the fundamental rights to a national culture and a language to national ethnic identity but may not, may not, and should not call in question his civic loyalty to the republic in which he lives as a citizen, in which, as a sovereign state, he lives as a citizen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this same binder, in the section which I called "Petkovic," and that is section number -- number 7. In fact, it is the second binder. It would have to be the second binder, if it is number 7. I apologise. Yes, it is binder 2. I would like to show you some documents which I also consider to be extremely important for properly understanding the relationship between the civilian and the military authorities of Herceg-Bosna and to what the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina -- the Muslim population. Look at document 2D1295. That is an order for defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the Usher to assist General Praljak to find these documents. It is topic number 7 in binder number two. Title number 7, second section in the second binder. I apologise for this mix-up, and I apologise for not being able to follow the prepared schedule, the prepared sequence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Anyway, General, you can see on the screen what I'm going to ask you about. This is a defence order for the so-called Operation Bura, which was drawn up in the Main Staff of the HVO and signed and adopted by Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic. Tell us, General, do you know this document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we read the definition of the enemy as defined in this document, we can conclude that the enemy is the army of the Republika Srpska; is that so, General?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If under item 3 we analyse who were the neighbours of the HVO at that particular point in time, we shall see that they were the Croatian army partly and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the other hand; is that correct, General?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The South Croatian army on the Croatian border.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we look at item 5, we can see that it refers to the Mostar Brigade, which with a part of its forces is holding the previously-defended positions and is placing a part of its forces at the disposal of the 3rd Brigade of the HVO. My question, Mr. Praljak, is this: What army -- what army is the Mostar Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Madam Alaburic. This was a joint action of the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I actually wanted to point to that collectivity of action. Now I wish to draw attention to other documents, 4D1700, so 4D1700. That is also a defence order of the operations zone of Central Bosnia, issued by Tihomir Blaskic, approved by Milivoj Petkovic. Regrettably, the document does not bear a date, but I believe that we can conclude on the basis of the context that it is 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you have read this document, tell us, General, is it 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, given the situation on the ground, was this order prepared after the fall of Jajce?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you get in touch with Mr. Blaskic regarding the preparation of this order and then analysis of the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Please, Mr. Praljak, do not answer immediately yes. Wait two minutes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: General Praljak, item 5 refers to the tasks of the individual units. I have tried to go through all these items, and if I saw correctly, all these items actually define the task in coordination, in concerted action with the forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In other words, it refers to the joint actions of the HVO and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So it refers to coordinated, concerted action. General, was it really planned thus, and was it really implemented thus?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to the next document 4D475. This is it an active defence order from February 1993, adopted in that year by Miljenko Lasic, the commander of the South-East Herzegovina operations zone. Let us look first and foremost at the definition of the enemy. It refers to the Hercegovina Corps, and to make a long story short, if you have read the document, can you tell us, it was the Army of the Republika Srpska that was defined as the enemy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of the Republika Srpska was defined as the enemy. The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was a friendly army, the same army as the HVO. They were jointly fighting against the joint enemy, and that is the sense of this document, and there is nothing to be added to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You had seen this document before, I assume, and you are familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, I apologise. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. General Praljak, I will now ask you -- actually, I have prepared a series of documents about Mostar dealing with the establishment of a line of disengagement about the conflict on the 9th of May and the situation on the 30th of June, but as my time is expiring, I will ask you a number of questions which are legally of exceptional significance for us, and they concern the shelling of East Mostar. Please, although you have already spoken about this, I should like to ask you to give us precise explanations, to tell us very precisely whether the HVO, in shelling -- in firing shells, was it under the obligation to target exclusively specifically-chosen military targets?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO only and exclusively responded to attacks by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the number of even thus fired shells was the minimum of minimums from a military standpoint. Selectivity was total. Even those military targets in Mostar which it was permitted to target, were not targeted, precisely because they were among civilian areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I can conclude on the basis of this answer that at the time of what is referred to as the shelling of Eastern Mostar, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was taking military activities against the HVO on the right bank of Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incessantly during the period whilst I was commander and also before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mrs. Alaburic. We will have to stop, because the Popovic case is taking place in this courtroom. I don't like it when people overstep their time, and when it happens to me, I complain about it. So you will have ten minutes left, which means that between now and Monday, you will be able to review your most salient questions rather than doing things in a hurried manner. Once you have finished, I believe it's Mr. Coric's counsel who will take the floor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is our turn, Your Honours, after colleague Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thank you, and we will continue on Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you will have the end of the week to have a rest. It must be exhausting for you since you have been answering all these questions without fail. In the few minutes that we have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... this morning. You did say good morning to all the others, but you left me out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are so present in my mind that I must have forgotten. Very well. I wish you all a pleasant afternoon. See you on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 6th day of July, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: [The Accused Prlic and Coric not present]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
